provenance: AI-assisted development expectations, written BEFORE the run. They are not independent human ground truth, not a labelled test set and not an accuracy measure: a disagreement can mean the expectation is wrong.
scope: development only; stored evidence only; no search, no fetch. Held-out questions and examples are not used.
unavailable: Original-versus-revision and explicit-revision cases need stored evidence whose document says it replaces an earlier one. Only the networking evidence (stored Q02 runs) has that; the SQLite/PostgreSQL development evidence contains no such wording, so domain databases carries only the off-topic-milestone and non-date cases.

a1a2-v5.purpose: A fresh check of A1 and A2 after two input/handling changes: the semantic verifier no longer receives the question or subquestion (rubric attribution-v5), and the subject backstop no longer rejects a descriptive subject. The expectations are the ones recorded before the first run and are NOT changed; nothing is forced. If the verifier blocks A1 again, A1 is recorded as relevance not exercised.

domains.evidence: stored Q02 evidence in data/q02-compact-continuation.db (claims 6, 5 and 3, with their stored quotes and passages; the Q02 question is a development question)

cases.kind: original publication versus a later revision
cases.subquestion: When was the original HTTP/2 specification first published?
cases.requirement: Original publication date of the HTTP/2 specification
cases.why: The claim dates a document whose passage says it obsoletes earlier ones. It does not say it is a revision and does not give the original date.

cases.kind: an explicit question about the revised document's publication date
cases.subquestion: When was the current revision of the HTTP/2 specification published?
cases.requirement: Publication date of the current revision of the HTTP/2 specification
cases.why: The same claim now answers exactly what is asked; the revision restriction must not apply.

cases.subquestion: What is the publication date of the HTTP/3 specification as an RFC?
cases.why: The claim is supported (a 2018 renaming proposal) but is not the RFC publication date.

cases.kind: a supported direct answer to a non-date question
cases.subquestion: Which transport layer protocol does HTTP/3 use?
cases.requirement: Name of the transport protocol used by HTTP/3
cases.why: The claim states the protocol by name.

domains.evidence: development claim-evidence examples CE01 and CE03 (SQLite and PostgreSQL pages, stored passages and quotes in evaluation/data/claim_evidence.json)

cases.why: The claim is supported but dates a later release (3.6.17) in a statement about test coverage; it does not give the initial release date.

cases.kind: a supported direct answer to a non-date question
cases.subquestion: What is PostgreSQL's default transaction isolation level?
cases.requirement: Default transaction isolation level of PostgreSQL
cases.why: The claim names the default level.
